title: Forschungszentrum Jülich and ARQUE Systems Secure €35 Million ($38.4 Million USD) to Build 200-Qubit Silicon Spin Quantum Computer - Quantum Computing Report
author: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
text:
Forschungszentrum Jülich and its Jülich–Aachen spin-off ARQUE Systems have launched Q-STAR.NRW, a €35 million ($38.4 million USD) initiative running through the end of 2029 to develop and integrate a semiconductor-based quantum computer with up to 200 qubits. Financed 90% through German federal funds under the Coal Regions Investment Act and 10% by the State of North Rhine-Westphalia via Forschungszentrum Jülich, the project will deploy the system into the Jülich UNified Infrastructure for Quantum Computing (JUNIQ) at the Jülich Supercomputing Centre (JSC).

Building on ARQUE Systems’ prior integration of a five-qubit prototype into JUNIQ, the processor encodes quantum information in the spins of individual electrons trapped in silicon and silicon–germanium structures. Rather than relying on fixed nearest-neighbor couplings and dedicated control lines for every qubit, ARQUE Systems’ patented shuttling architecture transports electrons across the chip to shared interaction and control zones, reducing wiring overhead and targeting long-term scaling beyond ten million qubits on a two-by-two-centimeter die.

Alongside hardware fabrication, the project partners will develop hybrid quantum-HPC software stacks, algorithms, and user-support services to connect the 200-qubit processor with JSC’s classical supercomputers. The resulting infrastructure will provide academic researchers and small and medium-sized enterprises with access to test applications in materials development, chemistry, pharmaceuticals, and logistics across the Rhenish mining region.

Read Forschungszentrum Jülich’s press release here. Related QCR coverage includes our earlier reports on JUNIQ’s initial integration of ARQUE Systems’ processor here and the Jülich Supercomputing Centre’s NVIDIA DGX Quantum deployment with Quantum Machines and ARQUE Systems here.
